title: Robotics technologist
_note: Technical round built from the Robotics technologist tasks in content/reference/occupations.json, which the team wrote from the eMASCO title (emasco.mohr.gov.my/masco/2144-06) and has not yet checked against the eMASCO task list. Behavioural round: behavioural.json. Rubric format: content/interview/sets.ts.

questions.text: Tell us about a robot or automated machine you built or programmed. How did you test that it worked?
questions.why: robotics technologists build machines that must work safely and reliably.
questions.source: 2144-06 task 1 (content/reference/occupations.json): Build, program and test robots and automated machines. Task written by the team from the eMASCO title; not yet checked against the eMASCO task list.

keyPoints.point: measure it works and is safe

questions.text: A robot arm stops moving partway through a task. How would you find whether the fault is in a sensor, the circuit or the code?
questions.why: faults can hide in hardware or software, so method matters.
questions.source: 2144-06 task 2 (content/reference/occupations.json): Find and fix faults in sensors, circuits and control code. Task written by the team from the eMASCO title; not yet checked against the eMASCO task list.

questions.text: How do you make sure a fix to a robot's control code doesn't break something else?
questions.why: a fix that creates a new fault can damage equipment.
questions.source: 2144-06 task 2 (content/reference/occupations.json): Find and fix faults in sensors, circuits and control code. Task written by the team from the eMASCO title; not yet checked against the eMASCO task list.

keyPoints.point: change one thing at a time
